Audited both enums with an adversarial review pass: all 24 BackendCommand and 33 BackendEvent variants (and every field) are constructed and meaningfully consumed, so there are no dead variants to delete. Splitting per service buys naming, not structure: command routing is by urgency/channel (Authenticate/Logout -> controls, SetVolume -> volume watch), events flow through a player->session->library filter chain, and CatalogFailed/TrackFailed are deliberately consumed at two levels, so a per-service partition does not exist cleanly. Findings recorded: the SetVolume arm in handle_command is unreachable by routing (now commented); the ignore list in app/events.rs is intentional exhaustiveness documentation.
All children complete: services extracted (Catalog, Session, Playback), run() shrunk to playback lifecycle + shutdown (65 lines), enum split verified not worth doing.

Split the app into a resizable main window (1280x800, min 720x600) and a fixed 1140x720 sign-in window driven by session state via windows.rs. Signed-in launches open main directly from a synchronous store check; auth loss pins the sign-in window over the surviving main window as an AppKit child window (gpui 0.2.2 has no window modality) with both close buttons disabled until re-auth. Compact layouts below 960px/1136px are now reachable by resizing. Subagent-reviewed (3 findings fixed: persisted session failures, prior-state restore on failed app-change reset, single app-change modal) and manually verified.

Rail 78pt centred on the measured traffic-light axis (39); brand logo and nav glyphs land on that axis via animated leading padding (sidebar_row_pad); hover/selection became a real content-hugging pill (sidebar_fill_geometry) per the decided spec. Expanded state pixel-identical. Invariants locked by shared constants and 5 unit tests.
Fixed by the cadence-5ym pill restructure: the brand header hover pill is now sized to the actual row at every window width instead of a clipped pinned-width box.

Title/Album are flex_1+min_w_0 columns; fixed columns share constants between row and header, with the header moved into track_row.rs so they cannot drift. Ellipsis uses text_ellipsis+line_clamp(1) via ellipsized_line() because gpui 0.2's text-measure cache never recomputes truncation for nowrap text in nested flex (documented in code). Design change: Album no longer takes all space after a fixed 320px title; the two columns split evenly.

Goal already met by gpui's new defaults post-migration: inactive_frame_interval defaults to 33ms (30fps), applies only to animation frames (event-driven position updates unaffected), with a high-input-rate bypass for unfocused scrolling. Nothing in Cadence animates continuously during steady playback; measured 0.2-0.6% CPU unfocused. No explicit config added on purpose: it would shadow a well-chosen upstream default with no measurable gain.

Evaluated per site. Springs: API (zed#62778, Aug 20) postdates our pinned rev e0931d5 (Aug 17); adopting now would mean bumping ahead of gpui-component's lockfile, against our pin policy. Deferred to follow-up bead. Synced repeats: only repeating animations are gpui-component Spinners, which use plain repeat() upstream; phase-locking them is an upstream change. No continuous playback animation of ours exists to sync. with_max_fps: only owned animation is the short interaction-driven sidebar transition, where an FPS cap only degrades. Nothing adopted, by evaluation.

Migration complete: git gpui at e0931d5 + gpui-component main, all gates green, app verified live. Children: deps switched (hbe.1), API churn fixed (hbe.2), regression passed (hbe.3), pin policy documented (hbe.4), traffic lights derived not measured (hbe.5), throttling verified as default (hbe.6), animations evaluated (hbe.7).

spotify::ErrorKind + classify_error land the typed boundary: 429 extracts Retry-After from the reqwest::Response inside HttpError::StatusCode, 401/InvalidToken/NotAuthorized map to AuthExpired, 5xx/transport/Elapsed to Transient; run_with_timeout keeps Elapsed in the chain; NotAuthorized replaces the string bail. 5 new unit tests, all gates pass.

RateLimitGate inside Spotify: every Web API method routes through gated() which checks the gate, trips it on a classified 429 (Retry-After honored, exponential fallback 2s..60s capped, jittered), resets on success; RateLimitActive typed error classifies back to RateLimited. 3 gate unit tests.

Reality overrode the plan: Spotify REMOVED the batch GET /v1/tracks?ids= endpoint for all integrations as of 2026-03-09 (rspotify#550 marks BaseClient::tracks 'endpoint removed'), so batching is impossible. Landed the achievable part: resolve_track_uris now runs single-track lookups 4-at-a-time behind the gate, propagates rate-limit/auth failures instead of swallowing them as deleted tracks, and still skips genuinely missing tracks. Radio's 30-lookup case now fits its 20s budget.

Cheap revalidation: reload probes both heads (2 requests) and answers Unchanged when fingerprint (first-page ids/names + Spotify totals) matches the last reload; full walk only on change, fingerprint cleared on account switch. Window activation re-added as primary trigger behind the 5-min staleness window and the gate; 15-min timer stays as backstop. Rate-limited automatic refreshes log info and defer instead of warning.

Queue tracks an ended state: end-of-queue rewinds the seeker to 0:00 (UI+backend), Resume reloads at the seeker position (restore_context_track) since play() is a no-op in librespot EndOfTrack, Seek records position for that reload. Next-on-last-track stops audio; ended clears on every fresh load via commit_loaded_queue, on reconnect restore, and on session teardown.

Autoplay ships: when the playing track becomes the queue's last, the backend prefetches radio seeded on it during the song and appends deduped results, auto-advancing if the song outran the fetch. Preference (default on) in Settings > Playback, re-checked when results land; stale-seed results discarded; fruitless seeds remembered so pause/play cannot spam radio. Review ran (10 findings, 9 fixed, 1 accepted as deliberate rest-on-dry-radio).
